status.summary: Active, but unranked and unbooked. Mauricio Ruffy stopped him at 4:29 of round 1 at UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn (Jun 14, 2026). Reports say spinning kicks from Ruffy hurt and dropped him before the ground-punch finish. It was his fourth straight loss, after Dustin Poirier (2022), Charles Oliveira (2024) and Paddy Pimblett (2025). Pro record 23-11-0 (ESPN, UFCalendar); UFC 2-6. He is 40. He has rejected calls to retire and says he plans to keep fighting (MMA Junkie, Sep 18, 2026; BJPenn), and ESPN lists him as active. No bout is booked on Nov 6 (ESPN, UFCalendar). A fight with King Green has been floated in the media (Green called him out, and Jorge Masvidal discussed it on a podcast), but the UFC has announced nothing. On Nov 4, 2026 he appeared on WWE NXT as a special guest referee; Cageside Press sees no clear sign of a move to pro wrestling.

style.summary: An explosive, aggressive wrestle-boxer who goes for the finish early with big punches, a surprise front kick and quick takedowns into ground strikes. He has finished Hooker and Ferguson in the UFC, but he takes heavy damage. His 41% striking defence is the third-lowest of 120 lightweights with 30+ UFC minutes, and his output drops after round 1. He has lost four straight, three of them by stoppage.

moves.notes: Group weights (head, body, leg) each sum to 1. The engine's target split should come from fighters.json: recency-weighted landed shares are head 0.67 / body 0.22 / leg 0.11 and attempt shares are head 0.75 / body 0.17 / leg 0.07 (career landed the same, 0.67 / 0.23 / 0.10; lightweight median landed about 0.62 / 0.22 / 0.15). So he throws a little more to the head and less to the legs than the division. The head group leans on power punches (rear hand, hook, overhand) over the jab, matching his recorded punch KO of Hooker and his exchange-heavy fights. Headkick is small and stands for the front kick that finished Ferguson. The body group favours hooks because his body volume comes in pocket exchanges (28 body strikes vs Gaethje); UFC Stats does not separate body punches from kicks. Calf/inside is a generic split. Spinning is 0. Knee is low because only 2% of his landed strikes come in the clinch. Elbow is 0.1 for ground strikes, which are 24% of his landed. These weights are analyst judgment from the bout stats; no published breakdown could be fetched in this pass.

engine_notes.note: Damage intake: 5 knockdowns absorbed in 82.7 UFC minutes (0.91 per 15, about four times the lightweight median), 1.04 per 15 recency-weighted; 3 KO/TKO losses in 8 UFC fights.

Front-loaded output: in his three five-round fights (Oliveira 2021, Oliveira 2024, Pimblett 2025) his pace relative to round 1 is 0.78 / 0.63 / 0.59 for rounds 2-4. The round-5 value of 2.93 comes from one round, his late rally in the 2024 Oliveira fight (40 of 47 significant strikes landed and 1:59 of control in round 5, after 8 landed in round 1), and should not be read as a general late surge.
Opponents control him far more than he controls them: 260 seconds per 15 min against him career (313 recency-weighted) vs 169 for him; takedown defence 56% (median about 67%).
The dataset covers only his UFC run since 2021. His earlier Bellator career is not in the sums, so career rates describe him from age 34 on.
Recent landed output has dropped: 2.9 significant strikes per minute recency-weighted vs 3.8 career, though accuracy held (53%).
